mbm-2951.clue: The last question is always about the carpet.
mbm-2951.quote: After our favorite TV quiz finishes, Gran asks one final question about something in our room. Last week she asked which pajama cuff had lost a button. I looked down. The button was on the carpet and I'd lost my own quiz show.

mbm-2952.clue: My robot has a hem you could unpick.
mbm-2952.quote: I sewed a little canvas cover for my repair robot instead of painting its shoulder plates. The stitches are enormous at that scale. My workshop friends call it the robot that learned to mend itself.

mbm-2953.clue: A flat shell decides the innings.
mbm-2953.quote: At the beach I flip a shell to see who bats first. One day the shell landed standing on its edge in wet sand. We all took that as a sign to eat lunch before arguing.

mbm-2954.clue: My two claves don't match in the cold.
mbm-2954.quote: I keep one wooden clave inside my coat while we wait for the rest of the son group. The warm one and cold one feel different on the first beat. By the second verse they're old friends again.

mbm-2955.clue: My little sister paints the wake afterward.
mbm-2955.quote: My sister sits in the boat with a watercolor pad as I water ski. I draw a curve across the lake and she tries to catch it with her brush. My cleanest turn is hanging above her desk.

mbm-2956.clue: The pinwheel hole has a quiet minute.
mbm-2956.quote: Every afternoon the wind dies for a moment on our mini-golf course and the pinwheel stops. I take my shot just then. My cousin calls it cheating. I call it a good weather forecast.

mbm-2957.clue: I bowl with a spare pocket watch.
mbm-2957.quote: The old alley had a clock with no hands for a whole year. I brought my grandfather's pocket watch so we could catch our bus. Somehow we still always played one frame too many.

mbm-2958.clue: I learned the song between the songs.
mbm-2958.quote: At our traditional music session an older fiddler hums a little phrase while he retunes. I learned that phrase by ear and played it back once. He looked at me and said he'd been writing that tune for forty years.

mbm-2959.clue: I keep my stage rain in a coffee tin.
mbm-2959.quote: For rehearsal I shake dried peas in a tin behind the painted window. Our lead always opens her umbrella a second before the downpour. After the show she wrote me a note thanking the weatherman.

mbm-2960.clue: Our new puppet has the oldest eyebrows in town.
mbm-2960.quote: My grandad let me trace his eyebrows onto a paper pattern for a glove puppet. When he came to the first show he raised just one. I tucked my thumb into the puppet's brow and raised the other. A whole row of children tried it on their own faces.

mbm-2961.clue: We came home with a very fancy portrait of our knees.
mbm-2961.quote: At the end of our raft trip we wanted a group photo. I balanced the camera on a rock and ran back, but the stone tilted. Eight wet knees and the tops of our muddy shoes made the print. We framed it in the boathouse.

mbm-2962.quote: I cut little dark rectangles from a retired teacher's skirt and stitched bright schoolroom windows round them. Her former pupils each embroidered one white chalk mark. My crooked seven is in the last row.

mbm-2963.clue: I reserve my chair with a pirate flag.
mbm-2963.quote: I tie a black bandanna to my deck chair so my nephew can spot me across the sunny lawn. Every visit he demands a password and a slice of melon before he'll let me return to my book.

mbm-2964.clue: The blue seam took two summers.
mbm-2964.quote: I pieced one side of a blue lake during the last holiday with my grandma. When I finished the other side the next year I used her spool of thread. From across the room it's just one unbroken shore.

mbm-2965.clue: My model spends its afternoons carrying tea.
mbm-2965.quote: I built a tiny robot with a tray instead of a shield and glued a minuscule cup to it. It has guarded my full-size teapot through every difficult afternoon at the workbench.

mbm-2966.clue: The first patch is the size of a train ticket.
mbm-2966.quote: I started a quilt on a long journey with a scrap just big enough to cover my ticket. My friends sent scraps from the next towns. Spread out on the table it's the longest trip I never had to take alone.

mbm-2967.clue: I used the wrong blue on both arms.
mbm-2967.quote: I mixed the paint for my model twice and one arm came out the blue of the sea, the other the blue of an evening window. I gave the robot a lighthouse to stand beside. Now both colors look right.

mbm-2968.clue: The blue one is for the people across the street.
mbm-2968.quote: I juggle in the window while I wait for my morning toast. Across the street a night-shift nurse used to lift her mug when I threw the blue ball. When she moved, she left that mug on my doorstep. I still send the blue one up.

mbm-2969.clue: Our passwords are drawings of sandwiches.
mbm-2969.quote: My game saved progress with a string of symbols we could never remember. I drew the symbols as bread, cheese and pickles in my notebook. I know the last level is the sandwich with extra onions.

mbm-2970.clue: I measure my putter on the porch post.
mbm-2970.quote: My dad marked my height on the doorframe. Alongside it we marked the size of each putter I used at the little course. One summer the marks finally crossed and he handed me his old club.

mbm-2971.clue: I threw a bowl for a single plum.
mbm-2971.quote: My first attempt at the wheel came out only as wide as my palm. I set a purple plum inside. The instructor got a photograph before we ate it, and the bowl has held one piece of fruit ever since.

mbm-2972.clue: The tiny rivets are peppercorns on paper.
mbm-2972.quote: Before I build a model I sketch the panels and use peppercorns to plan where the big round rivets go. My little brother asked for the world's first properly seasoned robot.

mbm-2973.clue: My cuatro has a very small audience at noon.
mbm-2973.quote: I sit by the open window and practice one tune while the baker cools her loaves next door. She taps my last note on the metal rack. If I rush she makes me play the whole chorus again.

mbm-2974.clue: I know the long walk by the fence latches.
mbm-2974.quote: There are three gates on our favorite trail. One clicks, one creaks, one makes hardly a sound. My friend can tell which one I'm at when I ring home and let the gate say hello.

mbm-2975.clue: My brush rests in a chipped blue saucer.
mbm-2975.quote: I drew a tiny shore on the saucer so the wet brush looks like a boat pulled up for the night. I finish each painting by docking the brush and tipping a little clean water into the harbor.
